text: TDE decrypts pages the instant a query touches them, so memory holds plaintext. Always Encrypted closes that gap for specific columns — encrypted at rest, in memory, and in transit, decrypted only client-side by an application holding the key.

With TDE, memory holds plaintext the instant a query runs. With Always Encrypted, memory still holds ciphertext — SQL Server never has the key, so even a sysadmin can't read real values without the Column Master Key too.
An Always Encrypted column is defined with a Column Encryption Key and an encryption type, deterministic or randomized. The Column Master Key protecting it lives outside SQL Server entirely.

Deterministic allows equality and joins, not LIKE or ranges. Randomized is more secure but doesn't even support equality server-side. Secure enclaves change the trade — a protected region where code briefly sees plaintext, invisible to everyone outside it, including the DBA.

Always Encrypted trades server-side computation for a stronger guarantee — the server never needs to be trusted with plaintext. Next up: Dynamic Data Masking, hiding results from ordinary, unprivileged queries.
